Priya: heads-up: polaris-8b int4 onboarding showing odd token insertions in code completions. tiny repro below. any quick ideas?

Nate: paste the repro + diff pls.

Priya: repro:
```bash
python eval_code.py --model polaris-8b --quant int4 --prompt "def add(a,b):
    return" --seed 11 --max-tokens 20
```
FP16 -> `return a + b`
INT4 -> `return  a  +  b` (extra spaces and sometimes missing trailing "

Iris: extra spaces often point to tokenizer whitespace mapping or a vocab placeholder at high ids. Did the conversion tooling change token ids or add a pad sentinel?

Priya: ran `scripts/vocab_audit.py polaris-8b` -> reports a token named `<PAD_[]>` at id 59999, converter log shows `--inject-pad` used by mistake.

Nate: that high-id pad can cause KV offset aliasing when the runtime packs caches; also check whether rotary/positional scaling was adjusted for int4. Try `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer as T; print(T.from_pretrained('polaris-8b').encode(' '))"` and also rerun without injecting pad.

bench-bot: perf snapshot: int4 polaris-8b ~42ms/token, ppl +1.3 vs fp16 on code-eval-mini.

Iris: also run `scripts/compare_token_spans.py --fp16 runA --int4 runB --pattern "\b\w+\b"` to see if tokenization boundaries differ. If boundaries are same, then it's probably logit smoothing/quant noise.

Priya: re-converting with `--preserve-ids --no-inject-pad` now. Will rerun `compare_logits.py --topk 10` after. Filing ticket ONB-4321 and assigning @Nate @Iris.

ops-bot: created ticket ONB-4321 and attached current conversion logs.

Nate: if mismatch persists after re-conversion, I'll bisect quantization clamp thresholds and rotary_scale (0.9/1.0/1.1) on dedicated pool. Ping me when logs are up.

Priya: thanks — will post results. :thumbsup:
